title: KV cache contamination detection probe and sweep
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: During a high-concurrency upgrade on 2025-01-24 the prefix/KV cache began serving stale/invalid values for a small subset of keys under specific interleaved insert+evict races. Symptoms: elevated 5xxs (service errors surfaced by downstream request validators), tokenization mismatches for cached prefixes, and unusual eviction churn. Impact: intermittent client errors and increased CPU/GPU wait due to repeated regenerations; roughly 4% of production requests experienced degraded latency or error envelopes for ~45 minutes before automated fallback kicked in.

Root cause hypothesis: a race between concurrent write/evict paths when a partial insert left a malformed tombstone-like entry; later, a secondary insert assumed the slot was free and rehashed incorrectly because the hash salt mismatch guard was disabled in the new allocator path. This manifested only under high parallelism and long-tail request sequences.

Mitigations applied at incident time: 1) temporarily increased eviction headroom and disabled the new allocator path (config rollback), 2) enabled strict validation flag that rejects entries with inconsistent checksum and forces regeneration, 3) rolled forward fallback to model-variant routing for affected routes.

Goals for this ticket: build a non-disruptive contamination detection probe that continuously scans live cache state for invariant violations, implement a safe incremental sweep to repair or quarantine contaminated entries, add telemetry/alerting for early detection, and harden the insert/evict code paths with lightweight invariants and additional unit+stress tests.

Deliverables: 
- contamination-detection probe (read-only, low-overhead) that emits per-shard contamination metrics
- incremental sweep job with rate limits and rollback capability (can quarantine keys to a shadow namespace)
- eviction scoring normalization patch to ensure deterministic priority under concurrent updates
- hash-salt audit and controlled rollout to prevent hash-mismatch on allocator path changes
- new cross-tenant load tests and CI stress harness reproducing the partial-insert race
- dashboards and PagerDuty alerts for contamination_rate, sweep_throughput, and repair_failure_count

Acceptance criteria: 
- probe runs in prod for 72h with contamination_rate < 0.01% without causing CPU > baseline+10%
- sweep repairs or quarantines contaminated keys with <0.1% false positive rate on a held-out corpus
- no customer-impacting errors in the canary region for 7 days after gated rollout

Notes and risks: sweeping in-place is risky; quarantine shadow-namespace approach preferred. Must coordinate with infra for memory headroom during sweep. Backwards-incompatible checksum changes require a migration plan.

Relevant artifacts: Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Contamination+Probe (design), GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2867 (probe), Incident timeline and raw logs: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/2025-01-24-kv-contam-log-archive
comments: 2025-01-28 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket created after postmortem kickoff. Attached incident logs and first-pass design in Confluence. Assigned to Marco for execution. Marking as P0 due to customer impact during the event.

2025-01-30 - Marco Diaz: Design review complete. We decided to implement a read-only probe first to avoid any write-time risk. Probe will track checksum_mismatch_count, tombstone_frequency, and stale_ttl_count per-shard. Draft PR opened: GH#2867.

2025-02-03 - Lina Okoro (reviewer): Left review comments on PR#2867 asking that probe use the existing shard-iterator abstraction and avoid allocating per-key objects to keep overhead minimal. Also requested a canary config to disable probe on low-memory nodes.

2025-02-05 - Marco Diaz: Addressed Lina's comments; updated PR with zero-alloc iterator and canary flag. Added unit tests covering synthetic corrupted entries. Pushed benchmark numbers: probe ~0.6% CPU at 95th percentile on a busy shard for 1-minute sweeps.

2025-02-07 - SRE (Jared Turner): SRE has reserved temporary memory headroom on canary cluster eu-west-1-canary for the sweep job and will monitor. Added runbook stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Sweep+Runbook.

2025-02-10 - Marco Diaz: Incremental sweep prototype merged to branch 'kv-sweep-proto'. Next steps: implement quarantine namespace and eviction-scoring patch, then schedule canary rollout window with SRE (ETA 2025-02-18).

2025-02-10 - Aisha Kapoor: Noted dependency on ENG-70213 (eviction-score decay fix) — we need that merged before wide sweep. Also requested security review if quarantine crosses tenant boundaries (holding security_review_required=false for now pending decision).
